niche.habitat: Damp volcanic tuff slopes, forest floor, and near fumarole seeps.
niche.diet: Decaying leaf litter, soft fungi, alkaloid plants, and mineral crusts.
niche.active: Nocturnal and crepuscular; avoids midday heat and desiccation.

body: A broad ventral foot and thick mucus coat minimize friction on rough basalt and trap moisture in thin mountain air. Coiling into a bitter sphere seals in water and deters predators with the same alkaloids that color high-altitude leaves.

links: Dense air holds moisture but high slopes bake skin
Mucus traps water and blocks UV

skill.effect: +30% UV and heat resistance; -20% speed; leaves a slick trail.

chains.weakness: Sea salt strips the coating; a salt line forces retreat.

plausibility.summary: State that alkaloids are diet-sequestered from red-veined meadow and slope forbs (F25–F26), like nudibranchs from sponges—not fully endogenous synthesis; keep iridescence from mucus glycoproteins and embedded grit (gastroliths, F23), not magic shielding.
fixes: State that alkaloids are diet-sequestered from red-veined meadow and slope forbs (F25–F26), like nudibranchs from sponges—not fully endogenous synthesis; keep iridescence from mucus glycoproteins and embedded grit (gastroliths, F23), not magic shielding.

analogues.organism: Terrestrial slugs and snails (Limax, Arion, Helix): pedal and body mucus limits evaporative water loss and lubricates locomotion on rough substrata; some lineages concentrate plant/toxin-derived compounds in slime for defence (from memory, unverified). Hawaiian food-web context: slow diffusion lengthens usable scent/chemical cues in still air (F16) parallels extended trail-following ecology in gastropods.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

skill.effect: Reveals creature path within 60 m for 30 s; marks targets for allies.

chains.weakness: Heavy rain washes gradients; crossing running water breaks the link.

journal.en: It reads the road after the traveller.

plausibility.summary: Cap reliable path reconstruction at ~25–40 m in still dawn/fog unless the target left a mucus or urine line; reserve 60 m for marked seeps/wind-aligned corridors. Note F16’s slower diffusion (~0.6× Earth) lengthens trail persistence in still air but slows update rate—tentacles should ‘scan’ longer, not teleport knowledge.
fixes: Cap reliable path reconstruction at ~25–40 m in still dawn/fog unless the target left a mucus or urine line; reserve 60 m for marked seeps/wind-aligned corridors. Note F16’s slower diffusion (~0.6× Earth) lengthens trail persistence in still air but slows update rate—tentacles should ‘scan’ longer, not teleport knowledge.

analogues.organism: Gastropod superior (olfactory) tentacles and lip chemoreception—tracking conspecific and predator trails on mucus ribbons (Chase, 2002, Behavioural Neuroscience of Gastropods; from memory, unverified). Leopard slug (Limax maximus) trail-following and mate/localization via slime cues; earthworm-style gradient crawling is a convergent analog on chemotaxis, not homologous.

chains.trait: Contractile body coils into a bitter mucus sphere
links: Contracts to expose only wet, tough skin
Alkaloid-rich mucus triggers predator gag reflex

skill.effect: -40% damage taken for 10 s; cannot move or attack.

chains.weakness: Flipping it exposes a soft ventral patch for 3 s before it can re-coil.

journal.en: It answers violence by becoming a stone.

plausibility.summary: Replace ‘stone sphere’ with a tight dorsal knot: head and mantle tucked, foot shielded, copious bitter slime plug—not a uniform ball like a pill millipede (wrong clade). Gag/bitterness from sequestered alkaloids + allomones in slime; 10 s immobility costs water and mucus budget (expensive on dry east-meadow afternoons, F18).
fixes: Replace ‘stone sphere’ with a tight dorsal knot: head and mantle tucked, foot shielded, copious bitter slime plug—not a uniform ball like a pill millipede (wrong clade). Gag/bitterness from sequestered alkaloids + allomones in slime; 10 s immobility costs water and mucus budget (expensive on dry east-meadow afternoons, F18).

analogues.organism: Defensive mucus flooding in Ariolimax columbianus and related slugs (thick, distasteful secretion when poked); partial body shortening/knotting under threat (gastropod reflex). Pill millipede (Armadillidium) enrolment is the convergent ‘sphere’ analog but arthropod exoskeleton—use only as behavioural comparison, not physiology.

chains.trait: Broad ventral foot glides over substrate
links: Small mass cannot overcome 1.6 bar drag
Muscular waves push against mucus-lubricated rock

skill.effect: +40% movement speed for 5 s; leaves a slippery trail that slows pursuers.

chains.weakness: Direct fire or concentrated salt burns the ventral foot.

journal.en: He does not run; he flows. The air is too thick to sprint.

plausibility.summary: Tie the +40% burst to a measured mucus overshoot (higher metabolic cost per metre, F4 sprint penalty returns after 5 s with extra dehydration risk); on bare andesite without grit, slightly lower bonus unless gastrolith grit in mucus (F9)—already hinted by observe cues.
fixes: Tie the +40% burst to a measured mucus overshoot (higher metabolic cost per metre, F4 sprint penalty returns after 5 s with extra dehydration risk); on bare andesite without grit, slightly lower bonus unless gastrolith grit in mucus (F9)—already hinted by observe cues.

analogues.organism: Gastropod pedal-wave locomotion on a thin mucus interlayer: muscular metachronal waves reduce friction on rock and glassy surfaces (Denny, 1980, Journal of Experimental Biology—mucus mechanics; from memory, unverified). Dense atmosphere increases hydrodynamic drag on fast whole-body motion but does not block low-Re crawling; mucus lubrication is the correct exploit for Babosa’s mass and F4 drag.

temperament: Solitary and slow, but fiercely defensive when cornered or threatened.
moments: Rain drums on basalt; the crawler uncoils, tasting the air with paired tentacles. It finds the mineral seep, leaving a glistening trail that evaporates before the sun breaks through.
